name: Spatial Variable Gene Atlas
description: Spatial variable genes (SVGs) reveal critical information about tissue architecture, cellular interactions, and disease microenvironments. As spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies proliferate, accurately identifying SVGs across diverse platforms, tissue types, and disease contexts has become both a major opportunity and a significant computational challenge. Here, we present a comprehensive benchmarking study of 20 state-of-the-art SVG detection methods using human slides from STimage-1K4M, a large-scale resource of ST data comprising 662 slides from more than 18 tissue types. We evaluate each method across a range of biologically and technically meaningful criteria, including recovery of pathologist-annotated domain-specific markers, cross-slide reproducibility, scalability to high-resolution data, and robustness to technical variation. reputation: A recent domain-specific benchmarking study that is useful for comparing spatial transcriptomics methods, but it is not yet a widely standardized community benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; performance is highly dependent on tissue type, spatial resolution, and study design, and reported metrics are method- and criterion-specific rather than a single universal score.
